Repeated Games and Cooperation

Play grim-trigger in the infinitely repeated Prisoner's Dilemma. Moving the discount factor δ\deltaδ flips which curve is on top — "always cooperate" vs "deviate once" — and cooperation survives in the shaded region right of δ∗=T−RT−P\delta^* = \frac{T-R}{T-P}δ∗=T−PT−R​.

R1−δ≥T+δP1−δ  ⟺  δ≥δ∗=T−RT−P\frac{R}{1-\delta} \ge T + \frac{\delta P}{1-\delta} \iff \delta \ge \delta^* = \frac{T-R}{T-P}1−δR​≥T+1−δδP​⟺δ≥δ∗=T−PT−R​

Examples & Exercises

In the infinitely repeated Prisoner's Dilemma with T=5T = 5T=5, R=3R = 3R=3, P=1P = 1P=1, find the threshold δ∗\delta^*δ∗ for grim-trigger strategies to sustain cooperation, and verify cooperation holds at δ=0.6\delta = 0.6δ=0.6.

R1−δ≥T+δP1−δ  ⟺  δ≥T−RT−P\frac{R}{1-\delta} \ge T + \frac{\delta P}{1-\delta} \iff \delta \ge \frac{T-R}{T-P}1−δR​≥T+1−δδP​⟺δ≥T−PT−R​
Show proof
  1. Value of perpetual cooperation: VC=31−δV_C = \frac{3}{1-\delta}VC​=1−δ3​. Value of a one-shot deviation: 555 now plus 111 forever after, VD=5+δ1−δV_D = 5 + \frac{\delta}{1-\delta}VD​=5+1−δδ​. Solving VC≥VDV_C \ge V_DVC​≥VD​ gives δ≥5−35−1=12\delta \ge \frac{5-3}{5-1} = \frac12δ≥5−15−3​=21​.
  2. At δ=0.6\delta = 0.6δ=0.6: VC=30.4=7.5V_C = \frac{3}{0.4} = 7.5VC​=0.43​=7.5, VD=5+0.60.4=6.5V_D = 5 + \frac{0.6}{0.4} = 6.5VD​=5+0.40.6​=6.5. Since 7.5>6.57.5 > 6.57.5>6.5 there is no incentive to deviate — cooperation holds. As δ\deltaδ shrinks, future punishment weighs less and deviation pays — which is why the curves cross at δ∗\delta^*δ∗.

Explain via the δ∗\delta^*δ∗ formula why a larger temptation payoff TTT makes cooperation harder to sustain, and compute δ∗\delta^*δ∗ for T=7T = 7T=7, R=3R = 3R=3, P=1P = 1P=1.

Show proof
  1. In δ∗=T−RT−P\delta^* = \frac{T-R}{T-P}δ∗=T−PT−R​, a larger TTT raises the one-shot gain from deviation (T−R)(T-R)(T−R). For T=7T = 7T=7: δ∗=7−37−1=46=23≈0.667\delta^* = \frac{7-3}{7-1} = \frac{4}{6} = \frac23 \approx 0.667δ∗=7−17−3​=64​=32​≈0.667.
  2. With δ=0.6<2/3\delta = 0.6 < 2/3δ=0.6<2/3, deviation pays: VC=7.5V_C = 7.5VC​=7.5, VD=7+0.60.4=8.5V_D = 7 + \frac{0.6}{0.4} = 8.5VD​=7+0.40.6​=8.5. Bigger temptation demands more patience (higher δ\deltaδ) — the formal version of "patience buys cooperation."
